title: Xor register: Positive proof strip
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: Maintain a register initially 0. XOR each nonnegative reading into it and record the register after each reading. Return only the strictly positive values in the derived sequence, preserving their relative order and duplicates.
descriptionMd:
A switch register toggles each indicated punch position as the ribbon advances. Neri prepares a clean proof strip for the front desk. Positive derived readings keep their places relative to one another.

Maintain a register initially 0. XOR each nonnegative reading into it and record the register after each reading.

Return only the strictly positive values in the derived sequence, preserving their relative order and duplicates.

Implement xorRegisterPositiveProofStrip(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Prefix bit state. Maintain a register initially 0. XOR each nonnegative reading into it and record the register after each reading. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.

referenceSolutions.python:
def xorRegisterPositiveProofStrip(readings, k):
    a=readings
    out=[]
    state=0
    for x in a:
        state^=x
        out.append(state)
    return [x for x in out if x>0]
